newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins dip with US Treasuries on CPI data.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins dip with US Treasuries on CPI data.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds eased, tracking a decline in U.S. Treasuries after fresh statistics renewed market fears of another U.S. rate hike later this month, dealers said on Thursday.

The U.S. April consumer price index (CPI) rose 0.1 percent overall and 0.3 percent excluding the volatile food and energy sector. Forecasts had been for rises of 0.1 percent and 0.2 percent respectively.
Like other emerging debt, MinFins are sensitive to any news which would suggest a further rise in U.S. interest rates, as this would push down U.S. Treasury bond prices.
"MinFins are tied to Treasuries and the figures have not been good for these. But trading is quiet as the market is waiting for May 20," one dealer said.
On May 20 the U.S. policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee meets and could raise U.S. interest rates.
An International Moscow Bank dealer said the fourth and sixth tranches were the most actively traded in an otherwise thin market.
Dealers said prices could ease further over the time remaining until the FOMC meeting as banks could prefer to have flat positions awaiting the Committee's market-moving decisions.
